title: Fiber Infrastructure
summary: Connect optical links, transceivers, distance, and safety boundaries to data-center connectivity.
objectives: Explain how fiber carries information using light.
Compare single-mode and multimode concepts at a high level.
Recognize attenuation, connector, and transceiver clues without performing live-fiber work.

vocab.def: A device that sends and receives signals, including optical network signals.
A reduction in signal strength as it travels through a medium.
A fiber design commonly used for longer-distance optical links.
A fiber design commonly used for shorter-distance optical links in suitable environments.

sections.heading: Light carries information
sections.body: Fiber uses light in a glass strand to carry information over high-capacity links. Different fiber designs and transceivers suit different distances and systems.

sections.heading: Safety is part of the skill
sections.body: Never look into a live fiber, handle glass fragments, operate a fusion splicer, or use optical equipment without qualified supervision. Classroom work uses diagrams, labeled inactive materials, or simulation only.

practice.prompt: A synthetic long-distance link shows rising loss and a connector warning. What is the safe student response?
practice.answer: Record the evidence, avoid live inspection or repair, and escalate to qualified personnel.

quiz.question: What is a safe classroom fiber activity?
options: Trace a simulated optical path and document its endpoints
Look into a connector to check for light
quiz.answer: Trace a simulated optical path and document its endpoints

lab.objective: Analyze a synthetic optical-link record and document a safe escalation.
